data.exact_reserve_text: The table below and on the following page show the Syndicate's cumulative incurred claims development, including both claims notified and IBNR for each underwriting year, together with the cumulative payments to date on a gross and net of reinsurance basis at the balance sheet date.

named_events.impact_description: Included within the Syndicate's RDS exposure; industry loss estimated and Syndicate gross and net impacts reported in USD (loss to the Syndicate of $206.7m gross and $26.6m net).
named_events.loss_description: This equates to a loss to the Syndicate of $206.7 million gross and $26.6 million net of reinsurance recoveries and reinstatement costs.

named_events.impact_description: Mentioned alongside other 2019 Japanese typhoons as drivers of large gross claims, reported in USD aggregated with other events.
named_events.loss_description: Gross claims for Typhoons Hagibis, Faxai and Jebi being mainly in Japanese Yen but any recoveries being in US Dollars.

named_events.impact_description: Referenced with other Japanese typhoons as contributing to a large JPY gross claims position with recoveries in USD; used to explain currency shortfall in JPY exposures.
named_events.loss_description: The large currency shortfall in Japanese Yen is partly driven by the gross claims for Typhoons Hagibis, Faxai and Jebi being mainly in Japanese Yen but any recoveries being in US Dollars.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2019 were GBP 126.111m. The syndicate recorded adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 6.5m (gross), representing a strengthening of reserves driven by development on older underwriting years (notably the 2017 underwriting year). The movement reflects large-loss and adverse claims development dynamics and uncertainty around reinsurance recoveries and foreign currency mismatches (notably JPY gross losses with USD recoveries).
raw_causal_phrases: The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.
There is always a risk that the assumptions and techniques used in these models are unreliable or that claims arising from an un-modelled event are greater than those arising from a modelled event.
The large currency shortfall in Japanese Yen is partly driven by the gross claims for Typhoons Hagibis, Faxai and Jebi being mainly in Japanese Yen but any recoveries being in US Dollars.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (gross +6.485m) was calculated from the gross claims development table (cumulative estimates) by comparing the 2017 column current estimate (148,483) to the prior diagonal (141,998). No explicit single-line 'gross prior year movement' figure was provided; a net prior-year release/strengthening narrative was not present. Some named event loss figures in the text are quoted in USD; amounts were not converted and are therefore left null in GBP fields.
